prompt: In a Nuxt project, which file is drawn at the address `/courses/:id`?
hint: A part of a file's name in square brackets is a parameter.

choices.text: `app/router.ts`, with a route listing `/courses/:id`
choices.why: That is lesson 12's list, written by hand. In Nuxt the list of routes is generated from `app/pages/`.

choices.text: `app/components/courses/[id].vue`
choices.why: A file in `components/` is a component any template may use, not a route with an address.

choices.text: `app/pages/courses/[id].vue`
choices.why: Right. The file's path inside `pages/` is the address, and the brackets make `id` a parameter.

choices.text: `server/api/courses/[id].ts`
choices.why: `server/api/` holds endpoints of the server, which return data rather than draw a page.

prompt: A page of the Vite planner arrived as an empty `<div id="app">`. What does a page of a Nuxt project arrive as, by default?
hint: Nitro does more than serve the API.

choices.text: The same empty element, drawn sooner by a smaller bundle
choices.why: The size of the bundle is not the change. The server now draws the page before the browser gets it.

choices.text: HTML drawn by the server, and no JavaScript at all
choices.why: The browser still gets Vue, and Vue takes over the elements it was sent. The page stays an application.

choices.text: JSON from `server/api/`, which the browser turns into HTML
choices.why: The API serves data to the page; the page itself comes from the server as HTML.

choices.text: Its HTML already in it, which the browser's Vue takes over
choices.why: Right. Nitro renders every page on the server, and the browser's copy of Vue then takes over the elements it was sent.

prompt: Which of these does Nuxt do from where a file sits, so that you no longer write it by hand? Choose all that apply.
hint: The table at the top of the section, and the paragraph under it.

choices.text: Make a route of every `.vue` file in `app/pages/`
choices.why: Right. The list of routes that lesson 12 wrote in `router.ts` is generated.

choices.text: Replace Vue Router with a router of its own
choices.why: There is still a router underneath, Vue Router 5, the one lesson 12 used. Only its list is generated.

choices.text: Let every template use a component of `app/components/` with no import
choices.why: Right. A component there is available everywhere, by its name.

choices.text: Take Vite's place as the dev server and the build
choices.why: Vite is still the dev server and the build; `nuxt.config.ts` passes its `vite` option on to it.

choices.text: Make `server/api/courses.get.ts` answer `GET /api/courses`
choices.why: Right. A file in `server/api/` is an endpoint of a real HTTP server.

prompt: How many files did `create-nuxt` make from the minimal template, before anything was installed?
hint: The `find . -type f` listing.

prompt: Nuxt 4.6.2 asks for Node `^22.22.3` on the 22 line. Which of these versions satisfies that range?
hint: A caret allows later releases inside the same major version.

choices.why: That is the version the javascript course installed, three patch releases short, which is why npm warned.
A caret stays inside the major version, 22, so 23 is outside `^22.22.3`.
That is earlier than 22.22.3, and a caret allows later versions, not earlier ones.
Right. `^22.22.3` is 22.22.3 or any later 22, and 22.23.4 is the release the lesson installed.

prompt: `npm audit` reported 7 high severity vulnerabilities. What did its report show them to be?
hint: Read the report from the top down: each line says what it depends on.

choices.text: Seven advisories, one for each of Nuxt's main packages
choices.why: The report names one advisory. The other packages are listed because each depends on the one below it.

choices.text: One `node-forge` advisory, counted along the chain up to `nuxt`
choices.why: Right. One advisory, and the six packages between `node-forge` and `nuxt` are counted with it.

choices.text: Seven separate flaws in `node-forge`, the package Nitro checks signatures with
choices.why: There is one advisory, and Nitro's `listhen` uses `node-forge` to make a certificate, not to check signatures.

choices.text: Seven copies of `node-forge`, one per package
choices.why: npm installed it once, in `node_modules/node-forge`; the other packages reach it through the chain.

prompt: Why does the lesson leave the audit warning in place instead of running `npm audit fix --force`?
hint: Look at what that command says it would install.

choices.text: `--force` deletes `package-lock.json`, and the exact pins with it
choices.why: That is not what the report says. It says the fix would install `nuxt@4.1.3`, a breaking change.

choices.text: The planner relies on the dev server's HTTPS certificate
choices.why: The planner never asks the dev server for HTTPS, which is why the exposure is close to nothing.

choices.text: It goes back to Nuxt 4.1.3, past a fix 4.6.2 carries
choices.why: Right. It trades a real fix in Nuxt's route rules for a warning about a code path the planner never uses.

choices.text: No version of Nuxt has a fix for it yet
choices.why: The report says a fix is available, by going back to Nuxt 4.1.3; what that fix costs is the problem.

prompt: In the transcript, clicking *Spanish* fetched `pages/courses/[id].vue` after the click. Why would a person reading the page not wait for that request?
hint: What does a `<NuxtLink>` do once the browser is idle?

choices.text: The server sends the code of every page with the first document
choices.why: Each page is a chunk of its own, loaded the first time it is needed, not all at once.

choices.text: The click loads a new document that arrives already drawn
choices.why: There was no second `GET /`: the router changed the page in place.

choices.text: The link fetched that code while the browser was idle
choices.why: Right. That is prefetching. `look` clicked before the browser had an idle moment; a person gives it one long before.

choices.text: The browser kept the file from the person's previous visit
choices.why: The lesson's reason is within this visit, a fetch made before the click, not a cache from an earlier one.

prompt: `/courses/spanish/extra` has no page. What did the Nuxt server answer, compared with the Vite planner?
hint: The first line of the transcript, before any script ran.

choices.text: A 200 with an error page, like lesson 12's catch-all route
choices.why: The status is real here: the first line is a resource that failed to load with a 404.

choices.text: A redirect to `/`
choices.why: *Go back home* is a link on the error page; the response itself was a 404, with no redirect.

choices.text: A 404, the same status the Vite planner's server sent
choices.why: The Vite server sent `index.html` for every address, and the catch-all route drew *not found* on a 200.

choices.text: A 404, where the Vite server sent `index.html` with a 200
choices.why: Right. Nuxt knows its routes on the server, so it answers with the right status.

prompt: You run `curl` against a course page of each planner. In which response is the course's `<h1>` part of the HTML?
hint: `curl` runs no JavaScript.

choices.text: Only the Nuxt planner's
choices.why: Right. Its server ran the page's component and sent what it drew.

choices.text: Both, because `curl` waits for the page's scripts to run
choices.why: `curl` runs no JavaScript at all; it prints what the server sent.

choices.text: Only the Vite planner's, whose pages are files in `dist`
choices.why: The Vite planner's server sends an empty `<div id="app">`; JavaScript draws the heading in the browser.

choices.text: Neither, since Vue always draws headings in the browser
choices.why: In Nuxt the server runs the component too, and the heading is in what it sent.

prompt: `app/layouts/default.vue` still has `import { version } from 'vue'`. Why?
hint: What auto-imports cover, and what they leave out.

choices.text: A layout is outside the auto-imports, which reach pages and components
choices.why: The same layout uses `<NuxtLink>` with no import; the gap is the name, not the folder.

choices.text: The auto-imports take Vue's composition functions, not every export
choices.why: Right. `ref` and `computed` come without an import; `version` is not among them.

choices.text: `version` is a type, and types need an explicit import
choices.why: It is a string shown in the footer, and types are auto-imported, as `Session` from `shared/utils` shows.

choices.text: An explicit import runs faster
choices.why: The lesson gives readability as the reason to write one; the build includes what is used either way.

prompt: One page should be drawn with no header and no footer at all. What does that page declare?
hint: A page names its frame in its own metadata.

choices.text: `definePageMeta({ layout: 'print' })`
choices.why: That picks `layouts/print.vue`, another frame. `false` is none at all.

choices.text: `definePageMeta({ layout: false })`
choices.why: Right. `layout: false` is no frame, for that page alone.

choices.text: Nothing in the page; `<NuxtLayout>` is removed from `app.vue`
choices.why: That takes the frame away from every page, not from one.

choices.text: A `<slot />` of its own in place of the layout's
choices.why: The `<slot />` is in the layout, where the page goes; a page does not leave its frame with one.

prompt: `app/error.vue` is drawn in place of a page and outside the pages, so it gets the planner's header and footer only when its template wraps its content in `<___>`.
hint: The component `app.vue` puts around `<NuxtPage />`.

prompt: Why does `planner.ts` go to `shared/utils/` rather than to `app/utils/`?
hint: Who else calls `toggleDone`?

choices.text: `app/utils/` is not auto-imported, and `shared/utils/` is
choices.why: `app/utils/` is one of the three folders whose functions every script may call.

choices.text: A file that exports types belongs in `shared/`
choices.why: Types are listed from these folders too; the reason is the server.

choices.text: Its exports reach the server too, and a route calls `toggleDone`
choices.why: Right. `shared/utils` is the folder whose exports both the app and the server get.

choices.text: `shared/utils/` keeps its code out of the browser's bundle
choices.why: The browser uses it as well: `SessionRow` draws its dates with `formatDay`.

prompt: In a component of `app/` in this project, which of these names are there without an `import`? Choose all that apply.
hint: Vue's functions, Nuxt's, and the folders the section lists; then the one name the layout still imports.

choices.text: `version`, exported by the `vue` package
choices.why: The layout still imports it: auto-imports take Vue's composition functions, not every name `vue` exports.

choices.text: `computed`
choices.why: Right. Vue's composition functions are auto-imported.

choices.text: `useRoute`
choices.why: Right. Nuxt's own functions are, and Vue Router's `useRoute` among them.

choices.text: `planner`, exported from `server/utils/planner-data.ts`
choices.why: `server/utils` is auto-imported into the server's code, not into the app's.

choices.text: `formatDay`, exported from `shared/utils/planner.ts`
choices.why: Right. `SessionRow` calls it without naming it anywhere.

prompt: `<___CourseCard>` is the same component, loaded only when it is first drawn, in a chunk of its own.
hint: A prefix of four letters, listed in `.nuxt/components.d.ts`.

prompt: Which file answers `PATCH /api/sessions/s4`?
hint: The method is part of the name, and the brackets are a parameter.

choices.text: `server/api/sessions.patch.ts`
choices.why: That answers `PATCH /api/sessions`. The id needs a part of the path in brackets.

choices.text: `app/pages/sessions/[id].patch.vue`
choices.why: `pages/` holds what the browser draws; the server's endpoints are in `server/api/`.

choices.text: `server/api/sessions/s4.ts`
choices.why: A file named `s4` is one address with no method in its name; `[id]` covers every id, and `.patch` names the method.

choices.text: `server/api/sessions/[id].patch.ts`
choices.why: Right. The brackets work as they do in `pages`, and `.patch` is the method.

prompt: After the PATCH, `curl` asked for `GET /api/sessions/s4` and got a 404. Why?
hint: The file's name carries the method.

choices.text: s4 was done by then, and a done session is hidden
choices.why: s4 was still there: the PATCH had just returned it with `done: true`.

choices.text: There is no `[id].get.ts` beside the PATCH handler
choices.why: Right. Only `[id].patch.ts` exists, so the 404 is Nuxt's own: no handler answers a GET there.

choices.text: The handler threw `createError`, since a GET sends no id
choices.why: The handler is not reached: it answers PATCH, and the id is in the path for any method.

choices.text: The route answers `curl` only when it sends a JSON header
choices.why: The PATCH from `curl` worked with no such header; the method is what decides.

prompt: You tick s4 with a PATCH, then stop the dev server and start it again. What does `GET /api/courses` say about s4?
hint: Where does `planner` live?

choices.text: `done: true`, written back into `courses.json`
choices.why: The handler changes a copy in memory, made with `structuredClone`; the file is not written.

choices.text: `done: false`, back to what `courses.json` says
choices.why: Right. The data lives in memory, and a restart puts it back to `courses.json`.

choices.text: `done: true`, kept by Nitro's storage layer
choices.why: The lesson names that layer as what a real planner would use; this one does not use it.

choices.text: A 404, since a restart leaves the data empty
choices.why: The data is copied in again from `courses.json` when the server starts.

prompt: The week's footer said 75 of 195 minutes done. After ticking the 60-minute session of the 21st and loading the page afresh with `goto /`, how many minutes done did it say?
hint: The tick survived the fresh load.

prompt: Why did the page loaded afresh with `goto /` still show the tick?
hint: Where did the PATCH make its change?

choices.text: `useFetch` kept the change in `localStorage`, as lesson 4 did
choices.why: The Nuxt planner does not use `localStorage`; the change is in the server's memory.

choices.text: `refresh()` wrote the change to `server/data/courses.json`
choices.why: `refresh()` asks the server again; it writes no file.

choices.text: The browser kept the page from before `goto`
choices.why: `goto` loaded the page from the server again, as a different visit would.

choices.text: The server holds the data, and each visit reads it with `useFetch`
choices.why: Right. The change is in the server's memory, so a second browser, or `curl`, sees it too.

prompt: `pages/courses/[id].vue` throws `createError` with status 404 when no course has the id. What does a visitor to `/courses/piano` get?
hint: The page is drawn on the server too, and `error.vue` asks for a frame.

choices.text: The planner's `error.vue`, on a response with status 200
choices.why: The page is drawn on the server, so the 404 is the status of the response, not only a message on the screen.

choices.text: An empty page, as the error is thrown before the template
choices.why: Nuxt draws `error.vue` in place of the page that threw.

choices.text: `error.vue` in the planner's frame, on a 404
choices.why: Right. *No course called piano*, inside the layout, and a 404 as the HTTP status.

choices.text: Nuxt's own error page, outside the planner's frame, on a 404
choices.why: The planner's `error.vue` replaced Nuxt's, and it wraps itself in `<NuxtLayout>`.

choices.text: `GET /courses/spanish/extra`

choices.text: `GET /courses/guitar`

choices.text: `GET /api/sessions/s4`

prompt: To the finished project you add `app/pages/settings.vue` and `server/api/settings.get.ts`. What answers now that did not before?
hint: One folder makes pages, the other endpoints, and each has its own prefix.

choices.text: The page `/settings`, once it is listed in a router file

choices.text: The page `/settings` and `GET /api/settings`

choices.text: `/settings` alone, the page and the endpoint sharing that one address
